title: Sikhye Sweet Rice Punch
shortDescription: Cooked rice and commercial barley malt liquid are held in a verified hot range until sweet, then boiled fully, rapidly cooled, and served cold.
culturalContext: Sikhye is a traditional Korean sweet rice drink made by using barley malt enzymes to sweeten cooked rice, then boiling and chilling the drink. Household sweetness, rice handling, ginger, and garnish vary; it is not an alcoholic fermentation.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Temperature-controlled rice cooker or slow cooker

instructions.heading: Extract malt liquid
instructions.action: Mix malt powder with cool water, rest 20 minutes, then strain through a fine mesh without forcing sediment through.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Liquid is tan with most solids removed.
instructions.safetyNote: Verify the malt label for barley/wheat gluten and use clean equipment.

instructions.heading: Combine hot
instructions.action: Place freshly cooked hot rice and strained malt liquid in a temperature-controlled appliance.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not use an unverified warm setting; measure the liquid temperature with a calibrated probe.

instructions.heading: Hold in verified range
instructions.action: Hold 4 to 5 hours, checking hourly, until several rice grains float and the liquid tastes mildly sweet.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Several grains float and liquid is sweet.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep at or above 140°F / 60°C throughout; if control is lost, discard rather than continue at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Boil fully
instructions.action: Transfer to a large pot, add sugar and optional ginger, and bring the entire batch to a rolling boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Entire surface boils and sugar dissolves.
instructions.safetyNote: Prevent steam and sugar-syrup burns; keep the pot attended.

instructions.heading: Cool rapidly
instructions.action: Divide into shallow containers and set them in an ice bath, stirring with a clean utensil until cold, then cover and refrigerate.
instructions.temperature: Cool from 140 to 70°F / 60 to 21°C within 2 hours and to 40°F / 4°C within 4 more hours
instructions.safetyNote: Cooked rice can support bacterial growth; do not cool the full pot at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Serve cold
instructions.action: Serve cold with a clean ladle and optional verified pine-nut garnish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Drink is cold with rice grains suspended.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep cold during service; identify gluten and optional tree-nut allergens.

grillSetup: No grill required; use a verified temperature-controlled appliance, stable stovetop, and rapid-cooling setup.
targetInternalTemperature: Hold at 140 to 150°F / 60 to 66°C during enzyme conversion, boil the full batch, then cool to 40°F / 4°C or below within the stated two-stage limit.
visualDonenessCues: Several rice grains float during the verified hot hold
Full batch reaches a rolling boil
Drink is rapidly cooled to 40°F / 4°C or below
foodSafetyNotes: Sikhye is an enzyme-sweetened cooked-rice drink, not an alcoholic fermentation and not a room-temperature process.
Verify the appliance maintains 140 to 150°F / 60 to 66°C; discard after an uncontrolled warm hold.
After the hot hold, bring the entire batch to a rolling boil.
Rapidly cool in shallow containers: 140 to 70°F within 2 hours and 70 to 40°F within 4 additional hours.
Cooked rice requires strict time-temperature control; never cool the full pot on the counter.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Omit pine-nut garnish to remove that ingredient, while still checking all labels for cross-contact.
Do not substitute an unlabeled malt product or alter the hot-hold range without test-kitchen review.
ingredientSourcing: Use commercial barley malt powder with a complete label.
Use fresh hot cooked rice and potable water.
makeAhead: Prepare, boil, rapidly cool, and refrigerate up to 2 days ahead.
storage: Keep covered at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 3 days pending test-kitchen validation.
reheating: Serve cold; if reheated for another use, bring to 165°F / 74°C and do not cycle repeatedly.
leftovers: Discard drink left above 40°F / 4°C beyond 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C; never mix service leftovers into the stored batch.
servingSuggestions: Serve very cold in small bowls or cups.
Offer pine nuts only after an allergen check.

faq.question: Is sikhye fermented or alcoholic?
faq.answer: No. Barley malt enzymes convert rice starch to sugars, and this method uses a controlled hot hold followed by a full boil.

faq.question: Can I cool the pot on the counter?
faq.answer: No. Divide into shallow containers and use an ice bath to meet the two-stage cooling limit.

metaDescription: Make sikhye with a thermometer-verified hot hold, full rolling boil, rapid two-stage cooling, strict cooked-rice control, and cold service.
